problem_statement: Let p be an odd prime with Legendre symbol chi, let m>=1 with (m,p)=1, a with (a,m)=1, and I=(N,N+H] with N>=0, H>=1. Let Q=#{n in I: n=a mod m, p not dividing n} and R=#{n in I: n=a mod m, chi(n)=1}. Prove a fully explicit inequality |R-Q/2| <= (1/(2*phi(m))) * sum_{psi mod m} B(q_{psi}) where q_{psi} is the conductor of chi*psi (dividing p*m) and B(q) is an explicit Frolenkov-Pomerance Polya-Vinogradov bound of the form C0*sqrt(q)*log(q), and deduce an explicit threshold H0(p,m) such that H>H0(p,m) forces I to contain both a quadratic residue and a nonresidue congruent to a mod m.
record_title: Explicit Polya-Vinogradov error term for quadratic residues in a short interval intersected with a residue class
